legend: You have a long fence which consists of n%%ZSMJ0%% sections. Unfortunately, it is not painted, so you decided to hire q%%ZSMJ1%% painters to paint it. i%%ZSMJ2%%-th painter will paint all sections x%%ZSMJ3%% such that li≤x≤ri%%ZSMJ4%%.
Unfortunately, you are on a tight budget, so you may hire only q−2%%ZSMJ5%% painters. Obviously, only painters you hire will do their work.
You want to maximize the number of painted sections if you choose q−2%%ZSMJ6%% painters optimally. A section is considered painted if at least one painter paints it.
input: The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ7%% and q%%ZSMJ8%% (3≤n,q≤5000%%ZSMJ9%%) — the number of sections and the number of painters availible for hire, respectively.
Then q%%ZSMJ10%% lines follow, each describing one of the painters: i%%ZSMJ11%%-th line contains two integers li%%ZSMJ12%% and ri%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤li≤ri≤n%%ZSMJ14%%).
output: Print one integer — maximum number of painted sections if you hire q−2%%ZSMJ15%% painters.
